label: Build your first agent
description: An AI agent that calls a tool. It fetches a random quote through the HTTP Client tool, explains it in one sentence, and logs the answer. Runs on a manual trigger, so click Run after importing.

tasks.label: Explain a quote
tasks.description: The agent at the heart of this workflow. It follows the system prompt: it calls the "Get a random quote" tool, then replies with the quote, its author and a one-sentence explanation. Its text reply is the output that the logger step uses.
tasks.name: aiAgent_1

parameters.systemPrompt: You are a friendly assistant. Always call the Get a random quote tool first. Then reply with the quote, its author, and one sentence explaining what the quote means. Do not invent quotes.
parameters.userPrompt: Fetch a random quote and explain it.

model.label: OpenAI
model.description: The language model the agent thinks with (gpt-5-mini). It decides when to call the quote tool and writes the final explanation. Needs an OpenAI connection.
model.name: openAi_1

tools.label: Get a random quote
tools.description: A tool the agent can call. It sends a GET request to dummyjson.com and returns a random quote with its author, which the agent then explains.
tools.name: httpClient_1

tasks.label: Log the answer
tasks.description: Writes the agent's answer to the execution log, so you can read the quote and its explanation after clicking Run.
tasks.name: logger_1

stickyNotes.content:
## Start here: run your first agent

The **Explain a quote** agent has one tool, **Get a random quote**. The model decides when to call it.

1. Open the **OpenAI** model inside the agent and add your OpenAI connection.
2. Click **Test** to run the workflow.
3. Click the agent and open its **Output** tab to see the answer. **Log the answer** writes the same text to the execution log.
4. Next, change the system prompt, or add another tool to the agent's **Tools** slot.
